title: AASI for Anxiety, Depression, and Related Conditions PATH

blocks.text: AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI) is a process that provides AMEs the ability to re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate (Authorization) to an applicant who has a medical condition that is disqualifying under Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) part 67.
blocks.html: AME Assisted Special Issuance (AASI) is a process that provides AMEs the ability to re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization for Special Issuance of a Medical Certificate (Authorization) to an applicant who has a medical condition that is disqualifying under Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) part 67.

blocks.text: An FAA physician provides the initial certification decision and grants the Authorization in accordance with 14 CFR § 67.401. The Authorization letter is accompanied by attachments that specify the information that the treating physician(s) must provide for the re-issuance determination. If this is a first-time application for an AASI for the above disease/condition, and the applicant has all the requisite medical information necessary for a determination, the AME must defer and submit all the documentation to the AMCD or RFS for the initial determination.

blocks.text: AMEs may re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization, if the applicant provides all the following:
blocks.html: AMEs may re-issue an airman medical certificate under the provisions of an Authorization, if the applicant provides all the following:

• 1. An Authorization granted by the FAA which states that AASI PATH has been approved;

  • 2. All interim Detailed Clinical Progress Notes (DCPN). At a MINIMUM, this must include:

    • a. EVERY 6 months (or more often as clinically indicated), progress notes from a clinic visit with a treating physician (MD/DO) or extender (PA-C/NP/midlevel);
    • b. At least one of these 6-month visits (and corresponding progress note) must come from a physician (MD/DO), such as a Primary Care Physician or Psychiatrist.
    • c. The most recent clinical progress note must be no more than 90 days before the AME exam;
    • d. Detailed Clinical Progress Notes must include a detailed interim summary; current medications, dosages, and side effects (if any); any changes in medication dose or type since last visit; physical exam findings; results of all testing performed; diagnosis; assessment and plan (prognosis); and follow-up; and
  • 3. Anxiety, Depression, and Related Conditions PATH Status Summary completed by the treating physician and AME.

blocks.text: AME must defer and describe in Block 60 what item(s) caused the deferral if the psychiatrist, treating physician, or AME identifies any of the following:
blocks.html: AME must defer and describe in Block 60 what item(s) caused the deferral if the psychiatrist, treating physician, or AME identifies any of the following:

• Any NEW “Yes*” answers on the PATH Status Summary;
  • Any new (or not previously reported) psychiatric symptoms, signs, or diagnosis;
  • Any new history of substance use disorder or FAA substance dependence;
  • Any progression (change in symptoms that persist despite modifications to medication and/or therapy) of the disease; and/or
  • AME, treating physician, or treating provider has concerns.

blocks.text: The AME must notify the FAA Aeromedical Certification Division (405-954-4821) if there is a significant clinical deterioration in my client's cognition, judgment, emotional stability, or insight.
